title: New analysis challenges Gaza famine, casualty claims using Hamas-run ministry data
description: An analysis of Gaza's Hamas-run Health Ministry data challenges claims of widespread famine and disproportionate civilian casualties during the war, citing population growth and mortality figures that its authors said contradicted widely circulated assessments. The findings, published by the Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council (AIJAC) on Oct. 27, were highlighted by The Washington Free Beacon on Wednesday. The figures indicated natural population growth of approximately 1.2% in 2025, with 50,227 births and 24,650 registered deaths, including 5,780 classified as nonviolent. AIJAC argued that the mortality figures contradicted the United Nations-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification's August 2025 famine assessment, which also relied on malnutrition and food insecurity data. Of the 24,650 recorded deaths, 18,085, or 73.4%, were male, compared with 6,565 female deaths, or 26.6%. AIJAC said the figures challenged widely circulated claims that women and children accounted for 70% of casualties, although the breakdown did not establish how many of those killed were combatants. Israel's Foreign Ministry amplified the findings, saying that Hamas's figures were “not a reliable source.” Israeli Ambassador to the European Union Avi Nir-Feldklein also denounced accusations against Israel, writing, “The Genocide lie. The Apartheid lie.” He accused Israel's critics of seeking to demonize the Jewish state and obscure Hamas's crimes. The figures used by media to shape the global debate over Gaza have frequently come from Hamas’s own Ministry of Health. A new analysis examines population growth and mortality and finds that the data tell a very different story from the one presented to the world. "The exception—if a letter is submitted bearing the signatures of a majority of MKs (at least 61 MKs) requesting to elect a speaker at an earlier date." "We will respect the Knesset members, and if a majority of them ask to hold such a debate, I will set it for an early date and no later than a week," he continued. "There will be no clinging to the horns of the altar," he wrote, using a Hebrew expression for refusing to give up power. "You can stop promoting conspiracy theories in the media." Yisrael Beytenu and The Democrats have sent Ohana letters asking him to put the election of a new speaker on the agenda of the 26th Knesset's first session on Tuesday, Hebrew media reported. The parties reportedly remain split over who should replace Ohana. Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad has proposed outgoing Opposition Leader Yair Lapid, the party's No. 2. Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman also backs Lapid. Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar is said to oppose Lapid's nomination and wants the post for one of its own lawmakers.

Rabbi Menachem Margolin, chairman of the Brussels-based European Jewish Association, wrote on X: “We stand with the congregation and call on the authorities to establish what happened. Everyone should be able to enter a place of worship without fear.” Unia, Belgium’s equality body, received 192 reports of antisemitism in 2025. That was down from 277 in 2024 but up from 121 in 2023. Annual tallies in the two years before that were below 100. Belgium’s Jewish population fell from slightly more than 41,000 in 1980 to an estimated 28,900 in 2021, a drop of nearly 30%, according to a 2022 report by the Institute for Jewish Policy Research. The study found that Belgium had fewer Jews than it did in 1946, immediately after the Holocaust.

Last month, the Board of Deputies of British Jews labeled the Greens a “racist party” over a party resolution calling Zionism a form of racism. One user amplified by Polanski suggested that the March torching of ambulances belonging to a Jewish group in London was a “false flag.” The term is used to claim that Jews or Israel staged an attack to portray themselves as victims or to justify war. That user posts under the handle “Karl Marx.” Another account Polanski amplified, under the name “Jeremy David Parker,” falsely claimed that Hamas mostly targeted soldiers in its Oct. 7, 2023, massacre in Israel, the Daily Mail reported, citing the report. The Green Party did not respond to the Daily Mail ’s request for comment.

title: Hebrew University of Jerusalem presents honorary fellowship to philanthropist Dr. Wallace Weber
description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem presented an honorary fellowship to Dr. Wallace Weber during its 89th Board of Governors Meeting on Oct. 19 in Jerusalem. Weber is a retired dermatologist whose specialty practice expanded to include several offices throughout Kansas. He previously served in the Gulf War as a flight surgeon with the 82nd Airborne Division, later commanding the 410th U.S. Army Reserve Evacuation Hospital in Topeka. He retired from the U.S. Army after 31 years of service with awards including the Southwest Asia Service Medal and the Legion of Merit. Weber supports scholarships and regenerative agriculture at the Hebrew University's Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment, as well as other initiatives. He held a volunteer faculty appointment within the dermatology division at the University of Kansas School of Medicine, where he also created and endowed the university's annual lectureship, Military and Catastrophic Medicine. Weber was commissioned as a second lieutenant through the ROTC program at Colorado State University in 1965. He earned his medical degree from the University of Kansas School of Medicine in 1969. Professor Tamir Sheafer, president of the Hebrew University, bestowed the fellowship with the following citation: "in recognition of his long-standing support of Israel and the Hebrew University; in acknowledgement of his deep commitment to agricultural research and regenerative agriculture; in appreciation of his contribution to a safer world through many years of military service; in esteem for his remarkable career as a medical doctor and as an academic; in praise of his tireless efforts on behalf of the Hebrew University in the United States; and in deep gratitude for his generous donations to student scholarships and water research at the Hebrew University’s Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment." In accepting the honor, Weber stated, “It is an incredible and unexpected honor to be recognized by such a prestigious institution of higher learning as the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It is with much satisfaction and fondness for the accomplished members and staff of AFHU, as well as the staff, faculty and administration of the Jerusalem and Rehovot facilities, that I can reflect on my support journey over several decades.” Weber added, “It all started with a suggestion by one of the members of AFHU. The warmth and enthusiasm demonstrated in the initial contact with Beth McCoy [AFHU’s previous CEO] will ever be fond in my memory. Her staff’s ever-present willingness to help problem-solve and make me feel valued as a member of AFHU plays a major role in my support of this institution.”

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc won 53 seats in the Oct. 27 Knesset election. The Zionist opposition parties—Yashar, B’Yachad (Together), The Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu—won 48. The Arab Joint List and Ra’am together secured 19 seats, leaving neither bloc with the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority. Eisenkot said he was working to form “a national emergency government” as soon as possible. He vowed to strengthen the “bipartisan foundations” of U.S.-Israel ties, adding that Jerusalem would remain “one of America’s most reliable and capable strategic partners in the Middle East.” Eisenkot said he looks forward to working “closely and constructively” with U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration. Trump endorsed Netanyahu on Oct. 18, nine days before the election, and again on Oct. 26, the eve of the vote. In his Oct. 18 endorsement , Trump explicitly linked further American action against Iran to Netanyahu’s re-election. “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” he wrote. To all our friends in the United States and around the world: The Israeli people have voted for change and to replace the current government. Our democracy remains strong and vibrant. title: Two suspected Ebola patients in Israel test negative
description: Two people isolated in Israel over suspected Ebola have tested negative for the virus, the Health Ministry announced on Wednesday. The two had been hospitalized after returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and developing a fever. "The tests were carried out in accordance with professional procedures and the accepted international guidelines for dealing with high-risk infectious diseases," the ministry said. It stressed that no Ebola cases have been confirmed in Israel. One patient had been isolated at Sheba Medical Center at Tel HaShomer in Ramat Gan. The other was at Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center's Ichilov Hospital. On Tuesday, the Health Ministry told travelers who develop a fever above 38 degrees Celsius (100.4 degrees Fahrenheit) within 21 days of being in Congo to stay home and call its hotline at *5400.

title: Israeli Health Ministry director-general to step down
description: Israeli Health Ministry Director-General Moshe Bar Siman Tov has informed Health Minister Haim Katz that he will step down from his role in the coming weeks, the ministry announced on Tuesday. Bar Siman Tov is leaving after about nine years in the post, over two separate terms: from July 2015 to 2020, and again since January 2023. The ministry said he will oversee an orderly handover. The official led Israel's public health system through the coronavirus pandemic, as well as the War of Redemption sparked by Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023, massacre, including caring for thousands of war casualties and receiving returning hostages, the ministry said. Bar Siman Tov is expected to join Columbia University in New York as a research fellow in the coming months, where he will study how health systems cope with national trauma, according to the ministry. Katz in the statement praised Bar Siman Tov's "significant contribution" to the Jewish state's health system. He said the director-general led the ministry "with professionalism during especially complex and challenging periods." Bar Siman Tov said he was leaving "knowing that the Israeli health system is strong, professional and prepared for any challenge."

title: Israel signs $170 million deal with Elbit Systems for advanced IDF artillery training center
description: The Israel Defense Ministry’s Defense Procurement Directorate (DPD), in cooperation with the Israel Ground Forces, has signed a 15-year contract with Elbit Systems to establish and operate an advanced training center for the use of weapons produced by the Haifa-based defense firm, the Israel Ministry of Defense (IMOD) announced on Monday The cost of the project is estimated at 600 million shekels. Elbit said the contract is worth 170 million U.S. dollars. The new center will support the operational integration of the Ro’em (“Thunder”) self-propelled artillery system and the “LAHAV” (PULS) precision rocket launcher system into the IDF Artillery Corps, Elbit said on Monday. The “Ro’em,” or SIGMA, is a 155mm, self-propelled howitzer with automatic shell loading capability and Iron Beam laser system mounted on a truck. "SIGMA is capable of automatically selecting and loading the required projectile, propellant and fuse and laying the gun to optimally engage targets," Elbit said. The LAHAV rocket system is mounted on U.S.-made HEMTT Oshkosh 8x8 trucks. Its independent sealed launch pods can be mixed and matched enabling a single vehicle to fire different weapon types and calibers. Deputy Director General and Head of the Defense Procurement Administration Ze'ev Landau said, "The agreement we signed is significant news for strengthening the IDF's strength and readiness, and it directly reflects the Ministry of Defense's strategy to enhance operational readiness, strengthen Israeli industry, and ensure a long-term technological and logistical response to the field forces.”

The Iranian Foreign Ministry said the measures were retaliation for London's part in what it described as the "U.S.-Israeli war of aggression" against the Islamic Republic. The ministry also cited Britain's July 13 decision to designate Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under its National Security (State Threats) Act 2026. It claimed the United Kingdom had provided "military and logistical facilities and bases" in territories under its jurisdiction to support the war. MI6 was listed under an Iranian espionage law that bans cooperation with "the Zionist regime," meaning Israel, and other "hostile countries." The navy and air force were designated under legislation passed to counter the U.S. designation of the IRGC as a terrorist organization. The ministry claimed the steps were taken "within the framework of the principle of reciprocity" and warned the British government that it would bear responsibility for the consequences.
